summary: Reclassifies RFC 1863, a BGP/IDRP route server alternative to a full mesh, to Historic status, and obsoletes it. It is informational.

eli5.summary: This memo puts an old idea for routers sharing travel info into the history books, since no one uses it anymore.

questions: what are alternatives to full mesh bgp
subtitle: A short memo that retires the BGP/IDRP route server idea because nobody ever built or used it.

tldr.problem: RFC 1863 described route servers as an alternative to a full mesh of BGP/IDRP routers, but the idea never materialised.
tldr.mechanism: This memo reclassifies RFC 1863 to Historic status and obsoletes it, noting that implementations of RFC 1863 route servers do not exist and are not used.
tldr.outcome: Alternatives to a full mesh are BGP route reflectors, BGP confederations and private AS numbers.

today: RFC 4223 is an Informational memo that obsoletes RFC 1863, which is now Historic. No later RFC obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What RFC 1863 Proposed
sections.content:
RFC 1863 describes the use of route servers as an alternative to BGP/IDRP full mesh routing. In a full mesh, every router talks to every other router; the idea was to cut that down by having routers talk to a route server instead.

The memo is careful about scope. The term "RFC 1863 route server" means a route server as specified in that RFC. Other uses of the term are outside this document.
sections.eli5: When many routers all have to talk to each other, there are a lot of conversations. The old plan was to have them talk to one helper instead.

sections.title: The Decision
sections.content:
Implementations of RFC 1863 route servers do not exist and are not used as an alternative to full mesh routing. For that reason, RFC 1863 is reclassified to Historic status, and this memo obsoletes it.

The memo adds that IDRP for IP has never been standardized by the IETF and can be considered obsolete.
sections.eli5: Because no one ever built the helper machines, the old plan is moved to the history shelf.

sections.title: What Is Used Instead
sections.content:
Current techniques that serve as an alternative to full mesh routing include BGP route reflectors (RFC 2796), BGP confederations (RFC 3065), and the use of private AS numbers.

Other, non-RFC 1863 uses of route servers are expected to continue for multiple purposes, but they are out of scope for this memo.
sections.eli5: There are other ways to avoid everyone talking to everyone, and those are the ones people use.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo states that reclassifying RFC 1863 has no security considerations. It is an Informational document and does not specify an Internet standard of any kind.
sections.eli5: Moving an old plan to the history shelf does not make anything less safe.

references.text: Haskin, D., "A BGP/IDRP Route Server alternative to a full mesh routing", RFC 1863, October 1995.
Bates, T., Chandra, R., and E. Chen, "BGP Route Reflection - An Alternative to Full Mesh IBGP", RFC 2796, April 2000.
